subject: Everett / Many-Worlds with Born-rule derivation dispute
dispute_handling_rule: The protocol explicitly forbids forcing a binary verdict. This case records the competing derivation claims with their assumptions and criticisms preserved.

twelve_questions.1_physically_real: Universal wavefunction only (wavefunction ontology). Branches = decohered components.
twelve_questions.2_primitive_variables: psi on Hilbert space; no additional ontology (Door D3: outcome semantics revised).
twelve_questions.3_fundamental_dynamics: Unmodified unitary Schrodinger evolution. FULLY INSIDE Cbp.
twelve_questions.5_definite_outcomes: All outcomes occur (branching). No unique realized outcome is dynamically selected - consistent with Experiment P theorem. Definiteness reframed rather than supplied.
twelve_questions.8_additional_inputs_beyond_Cbp: NONE dynamically. All additions are SEMANTIC/decision-theoretic (D3/D4 doors), not new physics.
twelve_questions.10_novel_predictions: NO (empirically equivalent to unitary QM). H2 FAILS by design of the framework.
twelve_questions.11_falsification: Not falsifiable relative to standard unitary QM without auxiliary assumptions.
twelve_questions.12_unexplained_remainder: The Born-weight interpretation problem (see dispute record); preferred basis handled via decoherence but pointer-stability controversies remain.

position_A_decision_theoretic.claim: Deutsch-Wallace derivation: rational agents in Everett must assign weights |c_i|^2 (Deutsch PRSLA 455, 3129 (1999); Wallace 'The Emergent Multiverse' (2012)).
position_A_decision_theoretic.assumptions: Decision-theoretic rationality axioms; preference structure on branching worlds; 'rationality' assumed meaningful across branches.
position_A_decision_theoretic.criticisms: Albert (arXiv:1103.3945): circularity of indifference axioms; Maudlin (2012): probability meaning of weights not established; Price critique: decision theory presupposes outcomes to bet on, but in Everett all bets pay off (branch counting vs measure dispute).

position_B_envariance.claim: Zurek (PR A 71, 016102; PRL 90, 120404 (2003)): envariance symmetry derives |c_i|^2.
position_B_envariance.assumptions: Envariance of entangled Schmidt-decomposed states; auxiliary 'swapping' symmetry arguments.
position_B_envariance.criticisms: Critics (e.g., Schlosshauer & Albert 'Quantum Decoherence' (2007) review; Barnum et al.): step from symmetry to actual probability measure still assumes probabilistic content of the reduced state.

position_C_self_location_typicality.claim: Saunders/Sebens-Newton: self-locating uncertainty across branches; typicality weighting.
position_C_self_location_typicality.assumptions: Measure on branch space = Hilbert norm; typicality measure postulated.
position_C_self_location_typicality.criticisms: Choice of typicality measure is itself the Born weight in disguise (Maudlin; Albert).

position_D_postulation.claim: Many formulations simply postulate measure m_i = |c_i|^2 for branch counting statistics (e.g., Everett 1957 original; DeWitt).
position_D_postulation.criticisms: No derivation claim - but honesty about input.

born_rule_dispute_record.instrument_conclusion: EVERETT_BORN_RULE = CONTESTED / ASSUMPTION_DEPENDENT. Every published 'derivation' relies on an additional assumption (decision axioms, symmetry-to-probability bridge, typicality measure, or direct postulate) that functions as the probability content. No derivation from Cbp alone. This is CONSISTENT with the Experiment P + hostile-replication theorem: within branch-preserving unitary dynamics, weights are fixed algebraically by initial amplitudes, so any 'derivation' must add structure OUTSIDE Cbp - and in all recorded cases that added structure is semantic/decision-theoretic, not dynamical.

scoring.compression: gain = 2.5; cost = 3.5; compression ~ 0.71. Range: 0.6-0.83 depending on how the semantic cost is weighted. Recorded as CONTESTED.

hypothesis_test: H1 N/A - does not escape obstruction (stays inside Cbp); dissolves the question instead (D3 door). H2 FAILS (no novel prediction).
